statement: Whenever find_peak_grid(mat) returns a result r, len(r) = 2, and, writing i = r[0] and j = r[1] as mathematical integers, 0 <= i < m, 0 <= j < n, and mat[i][j] is a peak of mat: for every x,y with 0 <= x < m, 0 <= y < n and |x - i| + |y - j| = 1, we have mat[i][j] > mat[x][y]. Equivalently, mat[i][j] is strictly greater than every existing orthogonal neighbor; boundary cells automatically exceed the outside sentinel -1 because every mat value is positive.
preconditions: Let m = len(mat). The input satisfies: 1 <= m <= 500; there is an integer n with 1 <= n <= 500 such that every row mat[i] has length n, so mat is an m x n rectangular grid; for every i with 0 <= i < m and every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= mat[i][j] <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < m and every j with 0 <= j+1 < n, mat[i][j] != mat[i][j+1]; and for every i with 0 <= i+1 < m and every j with 0 <= j < n, mat[i][j] != mat[i+1][j].

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, find_peak_grid(mat) returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or access an index out of bounds.
preconditions: Let m = len(mat). The input satisfies: 1 <= m <= 500; there is an integer n with 1 <= n <= 500 such that every row mat[i] has length n, so mat is an m x n rectangular grid; for every i with 0 <= i < m and every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= mat[i][j] <= 100000; for every i with 0 <= i < m and every j with 0 <= j+1 < n, mat[i][j] != mat[i][j+1]; and for every i with 0 <= i+1 < m and every j with 0 <= j < n, mat[i][j] != mat[i+1][j].
